name: h3-fault-injection
limits: A proof of concept supporting H3, not H3's test: proposal U6 is not registered, so this decides nothing and adds nothing to Holm. It measures state recovery after corruption, not H3's utility recovery (C6 minus C5 accuracy).

A projection fault is recovered by replay by construction: the projection is a fold of the log (packages/core/src/replay.ts), and the clean state is defined by the same log, so its recovery rate is a regression check of the replay property, not evidence for H3.

Every log-fault column is fixed by the fault's shape. The change rate is 1 for deletion and supersession because their targets are drawn from the read, and 0 for missing metadata because the read does not rank on the provenance ref. Recovery is 0 because the deterministic lints report and never rewrite. Verification detects every edit (next limit). Lint detection is 1 for missing metadata, because the missing-provenance lint checks for a blank ref, and 0 for the other two (the limit after next). The one empirical fact is the combination: the only fault a lint sees is the one that never changes the read. The per-place rates are means over the three operators, each exactly 0 or 1, so they are thirds.

Verification's threat model: the edit rewrites an event body without recomputing the chain, so it fails verifyChain (the check `engram log verify` runs) by construction of the hash chain. An editor with database access who re-chains the log gets UNSIGNED, the verdict every clean control gets here, so detection holds only against an edit that does not re-chain, or against any edit when a checkpoint is held outside the database.

Supersession's lint detection is 0 by construction: expired-validity fires on a passed valid_to, and both supersession faults reopen the window. Deletion is detected by a new orphan finding on an item that names the deleted id; no B5 item names another by id (its refs name session and turn positions), so deletion's 0 holds by the shape of B5's state.
The log faults are detected by the hash chain only because the check's logs keep it (card E1.6); B5's own runs keep none, so on B5's logs an edit is invisible to verification.

The read is C5's read with the question as its query, model-free; B5's model chooses its own query, so the read here is not the read of any recorded session. Accuracy downstream of a corrupted state is not measured.

B5's state holds no superseded version; the clean state adds one governed close per base, so the clean read is B5's read with that item replaced by the next-ranked one (on the pinned S split every read is still full at 20). The store is not faulted: the read and the lints read only the projection.

U6's variants not built: missing metadata is a blanked provenance ref only (every B5 item's validity window is already open at its end, and the schema requires its start), and deletion is removal from the projection or a deny in the log, not U6's other variant, an item retired without a governed event.
On B5's state an assistant turn names no model, so the missing-provenance lint already flags about half the items; a blank ref is a detection only as a finding the clean state lacks.
